summary: Build limbs from connected segments and explicit joint pivots so motion reveals construction.
objective: Rotate the proximal joint: all downstream parts follow while its parent remains fixed.
example_prompts: Build limbs from connected segments and explicit joint pivots so motion reveals construction.

principles: Keep segment length, joint location and skin silhouette as separate authoring decisions.
Use a rest pose with named proximal and distal parts; cosmetic deformation must not silently change the declared joint mechanism.
implementation: Place pivot nodes at intended joints, then offset segment meshes beneath them. Add the next pivot at the segment endpoint.
Expose one joint control at a time with authored travel bounds. Keep left/right naming explicit rather than relying on negative scale.
For a soft creature, choose a skinned mesh or overlapping stylized pieces and inspect the joint gap in bent poses.
observable_checks: Rotate the proximal joint: all downstream parts follow while its parent remains fixed.
At both travel limits, segments remain attached and the visible joint does not open an unintended hole.

known_limits: This hierarchy is not verified anatomical geometry, a joint biomechanics model or a muscle-force simulation.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt proportions, finish and presentation to the scene; explain deliberate departures from this guidance.

claims.statement: Scene graph children inherit the movement of their parent assembly.
claims.scope: Transform organization; the suggested limb segmentation is authored.
